findings.description: The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so database storage, snapshots and backups are stored unencrypted and no customer-managed KMS key is used.
publicly_accessible = true assigns the RDS instance a public IP and DNS, exposing the MySQL endpoint to the internet rather than keeping it in a private network layer.
The master username is the default 'admin' account name, making credential guessing/brute-force attacks easier against an internet-reachable database.

The master password is supplied from var.password and is also interpolated into EC2 user data; it will be stored in plaintext in Terraform state and is not managed by a secret store such as Secrets Manager.

No enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports (audit, error, general, slowquery) and no IAM database authentication are configured, so security-relevant database events are not captured and only static password auth is possible.
The EC2 user_data script embeds the database username and password (var.password) in cleartext; user data is readable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstances or from the instance metadata service.
No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains available and an SSRF in the PHP app could retrieve the instance profile credentials (which carry s3:*, ec2:*, rds:*).
No root_block_device/ebs_block_device encryption is specified, so the instance volume—which stores the plaintext dbinfo.inc credentials file—may be unencrypted at rest.
The instance is placed in a web subnet and exposes a public DNS name (see output), providing internet-facing attack surface for an application that handles database credentials.
The instance role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", far beyond least privilege; compromise of the web server yields near-administrative control of storage, compute, and databases.
The RDS security group allows all outbound traffic on all protocols to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data-exfiltration and command-and-control path.

The security group is created without description or explicit rules inline and is attached to a publicly accessible RDS instance; combined with publicly_accessible=true the network boundary relies solely on the VPC CIDR ingress rule.
The database endpoint is emitted as an unmarked Terraform output, disclosing the internet-reachable database address to anyone with access to state or CI logs.
